repair_log.new:
Apply the $\mathcal I$-envelope levelwise. Its monotonicity and
concavity preserve the corresponding test-curve axioms. At an interior
level, positivity and multilinearity of the nonpluripolar product give
\[
 \int_X\langle(\theta+\omega+\ddc\Gamma_\tau)^n\rangle
 \geq\int_X\theta_{\Gamma_\tau}^n>0.
\]
The envelope in this enlarged background dominates its argument, so
mass monotonicity in that fixed background then preserves positive mass.
Increasing continuity, \cite[Proposition~3.2.13]{XiaBook}, identifies its
initial level with $P_{\theta+\omega}[\Gamma_{-\infty}]_{\mathcal I}$.
Thus \eqref{eq:rays-kahler-transition} is a positive-mass
$\mathcal I$-model test curve.
repair_log.reason: Explain change-of-class mass positivity by multilinearity, followed by fixed-background mass monotonicity and explicit initial-level continuity.

repair_log.old: For the ample case with positive reference curvature, fix a smooth probability volume form and use the resulting $L^2$-orthonormal bases adapted to the filtration. The logarithmic sum estimate compares the weighted Bergman potential with the finite Legendre maximum of the $L^2$ partial obstacles, with error at most $m^{-1}\log h^0(X,mL)$. Converting to the sup-norm obstacles in \eqref{eq:rays-bergman-test} adds a uniform error $\varepsilon_m=O(\log m/m)$. The norm comparison and the two inequalities needed to pass to tail envelopes are proved in \Cref{lem:rf-bergman-norm-comparison,lem:rf-weighted-bergman-comparison,thm:rf-phong-sturm}. They reconstruct \cite[Theorem~9.2]{RWN14} and identify the limit with the Legendre ray, without assuming that a supremum commutes with a limit. Endpoint closure does not change the forward transform.
